date_note: Cryptopolitan says prosecutors announced the sentence on Tuesday, 24 November; the exact sentencing day is not given.
exec: A court sentenced a man to 47 months after he used an AI-generated voice to pose as a streamer and obtain roughly $260,000 in crypto from memecoin organizers.
geo_basis: court named in the sources (US District Court, Southern District of Florida); coordinates are Fort Lauderdale
impact: Roughly $260,000 in crypto was sent to the defendant, per Crypto Briefing.
org: US Attorney's Office, Southern District of Florida
plain: A Florida man was sentenced to 47 months in federal prison for using a fake AI voice and fake accounts to pose as a streamer and get roughly $260,000 in crypto from memecoin organizers.
summary: David Anthony Sanchez, of Port St. Lucie, Florida, was sentenced to 47 months in federal prison plus restitution, Cryptopolitan and Crypto Briefing report. He pleaded guilty to money laundering and aggravated identity theft. According to Crypto Briefing, he used fake social media accounts and an AI-generated voice to claim the streamer N3ON had agreed to promote a token, and obtained roughly $260,000 in crypto.
title: Florida man sentenced to 47 months for AI-voice impersonation crypto scam, reports say

validation.note: Cryptopolitan and Crypto Briefing each state the 47-month sentence, the guilty plea and the crypto amount; Cryptopolitan quotes Acting U.S. Attorney Klukas. The DOJ release itself was not read.

evidence.quote: A Port St. Lucie, Florida, man is headed to federal prison for 47 months.
